newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia July-Aug budget deficit A$5.47 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia July-Aug budget deficit A$5.47 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit was A$5.47 billion in the first two months of the fiscal year started July 1, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Monday.
This compares with A$2.73 billion a year earlier.
The monthly underlying deficit was A$1.92 billion, compared with A$1.43 billion in August, 1995, Fahey said in a statement.

Government outlays in the first two months of the fiscal year were A$23.42 billion, 9.8 percent higher than the A$21.32 billion for the same period in 1995/96, and compared with a projected growth in 1996/97 of 2.4 percent.

"The growth in outlays mainly reflects higher outlays on aged pensions, assistance to families with children and a decline in state debt repayments compared to the same period in 1995/96," Fahey said.
Cumulative revenues were A$18.22 billion, a 9.6 percent fall on the A$20.15 billion a year earlier and compared with a projected 7.0 percent increase for 1996/97.
Fahey said the fall was mainly due to lower company and retirement fund tax receipts due to a change in timing for tax collections.
The headline budget deficit for the first two months of the fiscal year was A$5.20 billion, compared with A$1.18 billion in 1995/96.
The underlying measure excludes asset sales and state government debt repayments, which are included in the headline figure.
